raw_response:
I will start from what has worked on my land in recent years and adjust a little, not make big changes. I farm only 4.5 mu, so every bag of fertilizer still matters, but with wheat-maize rotation and well irrigation, I do not want to save a few yuan and lose yield. I have farmed for 35 years, so I look at this in terms of yield target, soil response, and cost. For winter wheat, I will stay with an improved variety, keep fertilizer a bit on the safe side, and make sure water is available at the key stages. Wheat on our side of Hebei responds clearly to nitrogen, but if I push only nitrogen and neglect phosphorus and potassium, the stand looks strong early and then weakens later, so I will keep the nutrients more balanced. For summer maize, I will use a hybrid because the yield is steadier and the ears are more uniform. Maize needs enough nitrogen, but I will not go too heavy at one time; I will still keep phosphorus and potassium in the plan because the rotation removes a lot from the field over the year. Since some family members work off-farm, I will keep management practical: rotary tillage, not overly complicated field operations, timely irrigation, and a limited number of pesticide sprays aimed at the main risk periods. On 4.5 mu, stability is more important to me than chasing the absolute highest yield.
